start.question: What do you want AI to help with?

ideas-material.question: Will you enter confidential, participant, unpublished or restricted material?

writing-impact.question: Will AI only improve grammar and clarity?

options.label: No, it will draft or shape content

data-human.question: Does the material involve human participant data?

data-identifiable.question: Is it identifiable or potentially re-identifiable?

options.label: It is synthetic or dummy data

ethics-covered.question: Was AI processing covered by ethics, consent and the data management plan?

data-restricted.question: Is the data confidential, partner-owned, unpublished, copyrighted or culturally restricted?

analysis-impact.question: Will AI influence analysis, interpretation or a research decision?

tool-type.question: What type of AI tool will you use?

image-purpose.question: What will the image or diagram be used for?

confidential-review.question: Are you handling material supplied for confidential review or examination?

options.label: No, I am preparing my own application or output

ideas-ok.title: Generally acceptable with human judgement
ideas-ok.text: AI may support brainstorming or explain methods where no restricted material is entered. The final question, design and rationale must remain researcher-led and grounded in scholarly sources.
actions: Check for bias, omissions and overconfidence.
Record or declare use if it materially shapes the project.

review-exploratory.title: Suitable for exploratory support
review-exploratory.text: AI can help generate possible frameworks, themes, terminology and keywords. It must not replace the final review question, inclusion criteria or systematic search process.

review-search.title: Use with caution and human verification
review-search.text: AI can suggest terms or draft syntax, but database selection, final syntax, testing, peer review and documentation must remain human-led.
actions: Check subject headings and syntax in every database.
Document the final strategy and any AI assistance.

review-validation.title: Validation and human verification required
review-validation.text: AI-supported screening, extraction or appraisal can affect review findings. Use only with an appropriate validation and verification plan, and retain humans for final decisions.

review-synthesis.title: Human-led synthesis required
review-synthesis.text: AI may suggest themes or structures, but it must not replace critical appraisal, interpretation, methodological judgement or final synthesis.
actions: Base conclusions on verified source data.
Check for omitted or privileged perspectives.
Declare and document material AI use.

copyright-check.title: Check copyright and licence permissions first
copyright-check.text: Access to a publication does not automatically permit uploading it to an AI system. Check the licence, publisher terms and tool conditions before proceeding.
actions: Use your own notes or lawful open content where possible.

participant-approval.title: Approval is required before proceeding
participant-approval.text: Participant data must not be uploaded into a public AI tool. Use of an approved tool may only be considered where ethics, consent, governance, confidentiality and the data management plan permit it.
actions: Check the approved ethics application and participant information.
Confirm the tool is approved for the data.
Seek ethics advice or an amendment if needed.

editing-low.title: Usually low risk, but check requirements
editing-low.text: Minor grammar and clarity support is not usually material use unless it changes meaning, analysis or claims. Publisher, thesis or course rules may still require acknowledgement.
actions: Check the edited version against your original.
Verify quotations, citations and technical terms.

writing-material-use.title: Material use: verify, document and declare
writing-material-use.text: AI may support drafting or restructuring, but it must not replace intellectual work or scholarly voice. All claims and citations require verification.
actions: Substantially review and contextualise the output.

synthetic-ok.title: Generally acceptable for testing or learning
synthetic-ok.text: Synthetic or dummy data can be used for initial testing where it contains no real or traceable information and is clearly labelled as synthetic.
actions: Confirm no real data is included.
Do not present synthetic outputs as findings.
Record use if it shapes the final method.

low-risk-check.title: Generally acceptable with normal safeguards
low-risk-check.text: Learning about methods or testing workflows with non-restricted material is generally acceptable. Outputs must still be checked for accuracy and appropriateness.
actions: Verify advice against reliable methods sources.
Avoid unnecessary or disproportionate AI use.

analysis-caution.title: Use with caution and independent verification
analysis-caution.text: AI-assisted analysis or interpretation can materially influence research findings. Ensure the method is appropriate, the tool is suitable and outputs are validated and human-verified.

public-restricted.title: Do not enter restricted material into a public tool
public-restricted.text: Public AI tools should not receive participant, identifiable, confidential, unpublished, partner-owned, copyrighted or culturally restricted material unless explicit permissions and safeguards exist.
actions: Seek the appropriate ethics, copyright, privacy or governance advice.

approved-not-automatic.title: An approved tool does not automatically approve the use
approved-not-automatic.text: University protection reduces some risks, but the proposed use must still align with ethics, consent, confidentiality, copyright, contracts, data governance and the data management plan.
actions: Confirm the specific use case is permitted.

seek-advice.title: Pause and seek advice
seek-advice.text: The risk cannot be determined safely from the information available. Treat the material as higher risk until its classification, permissions and tool protections are confirmed.
actions: Do not upload the material yet.
Consult the relevant support service or project lead.

image-scientific.title: Use validated tools instead
image-scientific.text: AI image generators are generally not appropriate for scientific figures, quantitative visualisations or diagrams requiring factual precision. Produce figures from actual data using validated tools.
actions: Use reproducible figure or visualisation software.

image-disclose.title: Possible with accuracy, bias and disclosure checks
image-disclose.text: A conceptual AI-generated illustration may be suitable in some contexts, but it must be reviewed for accuracy, bias, copyright and accessibility and clearly identified where used.
actions: Record the tool, date and prompt.

publisher-check.title: Check the current publisher policy first
publisher-check.text: Publishers differ in whether they permit AI-generated or AI-edited images. Do not assume institutional guidance is sufficient for submission.
actions: Follow labelling, disclosure and permission requirements.

confidential-review-no.title: Do not upload confidential review material
confidential-review-no.text: Theses, manuscripts, grant applications and other material supplied for confidential review must not be uploaded into a public AI tool. Any permitted use must be explicitly authorised by the relevant process.
actions: Follow the reviewer or examiner instructions.

funder-publisher-check.title: Check current funder or publisher requirements
funder-publisher-check.text: AI may support preparation of your own output, but requirements vary. You remain responsible for accuracy, integrity, authorship, confidentiality and disclosure.
actions: Check current policy before use or submission.
Do not enter restricted information into public tools.
